```{r}
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART G: AUC per imputation (bootstrap CIs, B = 2000)\n")
cat("(Raw models used — standardization does not change fit)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

calc_auc_mi <- function(fits_list, data_list, label, boot.n = 2000) {
  mm     <- length(data_list)
  aucs   <- numeric(mm)
  lowers <- numeric(mm)
  uppers <- numeric(mm)

  for (i in seq_len(mm)) {
    if (is.null(fits_list[[i]])) {
      aucs[i] <- lowers[i] <- uppers[i] <- NA_real_
      next
    }
    pred_i <- predict(fits_list[[i]], type = "response")
    roc_i  <- roc(data_list[[i]][[outcome_var]], pred_i, quiet = TRUE)
    aucs[i] <- as.numeric(auc(roc_i))
    ci_i    <- ci.auc(roc_i, method = "bootstrap", boot.n = boot.n)
    lowers[i] <- ci_i[1]
    uppers[i] <- ci_i[3]
  }

  valid <- !is.na(aucs)
  cat(sprintf("%s AUC per imputation (valid n=%d):\n  %s\n",
              label, sum(valid),
              paste(sprintf("%.3f", aucs[valid]), collapse = ", ")))

  data.frame(
    model         = label,
    AUC_mean      = mean(aucs,   na.rm = TRUE),
    AUC_lower     = mean(lowers, na.rm = TRUE),
    AUC_upper     = mean(uppers, na.rm = TRUE),
    AUC_formatted = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]",
                            mean(aucs,   na.rm = TRUE),
                            mean(lowers, na.rm = TRUE),
                            mean(uppers, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_valid = sum(valid)
  )
}

set.seed(42)
auc_A <- calc_auc_mi(fits_A_raw, imputed_list, "Model A (Personality)")
auc_B <- calc_auc_mi(fits_B_raw, imputed_list, "Model B (Full)")

cat("\n")
cat("AUC SUMMARY (mean ± mean bootstrap CI across imputations):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Model A (Personality): %s\n", auc_A$AUC_formatted))
cat(sprintf("  Model B (Full):        %s\n\n", auc_B$AUC_formatted))

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART H: DELONG'S TEST (POOLED — raw models)
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART H: DeLong's test — pooled across imputations\n")
cat("Pooling ΔAUC directly via Rubin's rules (Li & Fine, 2010).\n")
cat("SE = |ΔAUC / z| from pROC roc.test() per imputation.\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

delong_results <- vector("list", m)

for (i in seq_len(m)) {
  if (is.null(fits_A_raw[[i]]) || is.null(fits_B_raw[[i]])) {
    delong_results[[i]] <- list(
      delta = NA_real_, var = NA_real_, z = NA_real_, p = NA_real_,
      auc_A = NA_real_, auc_B = NA_real_)
    next
  }

  pred_A_i  <- predict(fits_A_raw[[i]], type = "response")
  pred_B_i  <- predict(fits_B_raw[[i]], type = "response")
  outcome_i <- imputed_list[[i]][[outcome_var]]

  roc_A_i <- roc(outcome_i, pred_A_i, quiet = TRUE)
  roc_B_i <- roc(outcome_i, pred_B_i, quiet = TRUE)

  auc_A_i <- as.numeric(auc(roc_A_i))
  auc_B_i <- as.numeric(auc(roc_B_i))
  delta_i <- auc_B_i - auc_A_i

  test_i <- roc.test(roc_A_i, roc_B_i, method = "delong", paired = TRUE)
  z_i    <- as.numeric(test_i$statistic)
  se_i   <- if (abs(z_i) > 1e-8) abs(delta_i / z_i) else abs(delta_i) + 1e-8

  delong_results[[i]] <- list(
    delta = delta_i, var = se_i^2, z = z_i,
    p = test_i$p.value, auc_A = auc_A_i, auc_B = auc_B_i)

  cat(sprintf(
    "  Imputation %2d: AUC_A=%.3f  AUC_B=%.3f  Δ=%+.4f  SE=%.4f  z=%+.3f  p=%.4f\n",
    i, auc_A_i, auc_B_i, delta_i, se_i, z_i, test_i$p.value))
}

valid_idx <- which(sapply(delong_results, function(r) !is.na(r$delta)))
m_valid   <- length(valid_idx)

if (m_valid == 0) stop("DeLong: no valid imputations — cannot pool.")

delta_vec <- sapply(delong_results[valid_idx], `[[`, "delta")
var_vec   <- sapply(delong_results[valid_idx], `[[`, "var")

Q_bar  <- mean(delta_vec)
U_bar  <- mean(var_vec)
B      <- var(delta_vec)
T_var  <- U_bar + (1 + 1 / m_valid) * B
z_pool <- Q_bar / sqrt(T_var)
p_pool <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_pool))

r_L      <- (1 + 1 / m_valid) * B / U_bar
df_BR    <- if (is.finite(r_L) && r_L > 1e-10) (m_valid - 1) / r_L^2 else Inf
p_pool_t <- if (is.finite(df_BR)) 2 * pt(-abs(z_pool), df = df_BR) else p_pool
lambda   <- if (is.finite(r_L)) r_L / (r_L + 1) else NA_real_

cat(sprintf("\n  Variance decomposition:\n"))
cat(sprintf("    Within-imputation (U_bar): %.6f\n", U_bar))
cat(sprintf("    Between-imputation (B):    %.6f\n", B))
cat(sprintf("    Total (T):                 %.6f\n", T_var))
cat(sprintf("    Fraction missing info (λ): %.4f\n", lambda))

cat(sprintf("\n──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n"))
cat(sprintf("POOLED DELONG'S TEST (Rubin's rules on ΔAUC, m=%d)\n\n", m_valid))
cat(sprintf("  Pooled ΔAUC (B − A):        %+.4f\n", Q_bar))
cat(sprintf("  SE of pooled ΔAUC:          %.4f\n",  sqrt(T_var)))
cat(sprintf("  Pooled z-statistic:          %.4f\n",  z_pool))
cat(sprintf("  p-value (normal approx.):    %.4f%s\n", p_pool,
            ifelse(p_pool < 0.001, "  (< 0.001)",
            ifelse(p_pool < 0.05,  "  ← significant", ""))))
cat(sprintf("  p-value (t, df=%.1f):        %.4f\n",  df_BR, p_pool_t))

if (p_pool < 0.05) {
  winner <- ifelse(Q_bar > 0, "Model B (Full)", "Model A (Personality)")
  cat(sprintf("\n  ✓ Significant difference: %s has higher AUC.\n", winner))
} else {
  cat("\n  Models do not differ significantly in AUC (p ≥ 0.05).\n")
}
cat("──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART I: DIAGNOSTICS (VIF + INFLUENTIAL CASES — raw models, imputation 1)
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART I: Diagnostics (imputation 1, raw models)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

run_diagnostics <- function(formula_obj, data, label) {
  cat(sprintf("%s\n", label))
  cat("──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")

  fit <- glm(formula_obj, data = data, family = binomial())

  tryCatch({
    vif_vals <- vif(fit)
    if (is.matrix(vif_vals)) {
      vif_df <- data.frame(Variable = rownames(vif_vals),
                           VIF = round(vif_vals[, "GVIF^(1/(2*Df))"], 3))
    } else {
      vif_df <- data.frame(Variable = names(vif_vals),
                           VIF = round(as.numeric(vif_vals), 3))
    }
    vif_df  <- vif_df %>% arrange(desc(VIF))
    max_vif <- max(vif_df$VIF)
    cat("VIF (GVIF^(1/(2*Df)) for multi-level factors):\n")
    print(vif_df, row.names = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("Max VIF: %.2f  %s\n\n", max_vif,
                ifelse(max_vif < 5, "(OK)", "⚠️  >5 — possible collinearity")))
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("VIF could not be computed: %s\n\n", e$message))
  })

  cooksd    <- cooks.distance(fit)
  threshold <- 4 / nrow(data)
  n_inf     <- sum(cooksd > threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("Cook's distance threshold: 4/n = %.5f\n", threshold))
  cat(sprintf("Influential cases (> threshold): %d (%.1f%%)\n\n",
              n_inf, 100 * n_inf / nrow(data)))

  invisible(fit)
}

run_diagnostics(formula_A, imputed_list[[1]], "MODEL A — Personality (raw)")
run_diagnostics(formula_B, imputed_list[[1]], "MODEL B — Full (raw)")

output <- list(
```

## Additional Tests
```{r}
#==============================================================================
# CHUNK 13: POST-LOGISTIC REGRESSION DIAGNOSTICS (MULTIPLY IMPUTED DATA)
#==============================================================================
# Purpose:
#   Post-hoc diagnostics for both logistic regression models from Chunk 12:
#     1. Nagelkerke R2      — manual per imputation, averaged
#     2. Hosmer-Lemeshow    — mean chi-square across imputations (g=10, df=8)
#     3. Confusion matrix   — sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV at the
#                             Youden-optimal threshold
#     4. Box-Tidwell test   — linearity in the logit (imputation 1; Bonferroni)
#     4b. Part F2           — supplementary sensitivity check for the
#                             DBAS_Medications Box-Tidwell flag in Model A
#                             (linear vs natural cubic spline)
#     5. Class imbalance    — distribution; threshold approach (Klok 2022)
#     6. Part K             — ten-fold stratified cross-validation, pooled
#                             across imputations, with optimism vs. the
#                             apparent (Chunk 12) AUC
#
# Design decisions:
#   - AUC reported here is taken from Chunk 12 (per-imputation mean with
#     bootstrap CI) so the two chunks are consistent. The pooled-prediction
#     ROC is used ONLY to select the Youden operating threshold for the
#     confusion matrix, not to report a second AUC.
#   - All other diagnostics applied to BOTH Model A and Model B, raw models.
#   - Box-Tidwell run on imputation 1 (Harrell, 2015; van Buuren, 2018);
#     variables with min <= 0 shifted by +1 before log; Bonferroni per model.
#   - Class imbalance: no resampling correction (Klok et al., 2022).
#   - Cross-validation (Part K): within each of the m imputed datasets,
#     participants are randomly assigned to 10 folds stratified by outcome
#     (folds hold the stopper/continuer proportion roughly constant), the
#     model is refit on 9 folds and evaluated on the held-out fold, and this
#     repeats until every fold has served once as the validation set.
#     Fold-level AUCs are averaged within each imputation, then pooled across
#     all m imputations. Optimism is the apparent AUC (Chunk 12, fit and
#     evaluated on the same data) minus this cross-validated AUC.
#
# Reads from:
#   regression_comparison_results.rds   (Chunk 12; also supplies AUC)
#   imputed_datasets_efa_scales.rds     (EFA chunk — contains EFA_F1..F4)
#
# References:
#   Box & Tidwell (1962). Technometrics, 4(4):531-550.
#   Enders CK (2010). Applied Missing Data Analysis. Guilford Press.
#   Harrell FE (2015). Regression Modeling Strategies (2nd ed.). Springer.
#   Hosmer & Lemeshow (2000). Applied Logistic Regression (2nd ed.). Wiley.
#   Klok et al. (2022). JAMIA. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocac093
#   Kohavi R (1995). A study of cross-validation and bootstrap for accuracy
#     estimation and model selection. IJCAI, 14(2):1137-1145.
#   Nagelkerke NJD (1991). Biometrika, 78(3):691-692.
#   Rubin DB (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley.
#   van Buuren S (2018). Flexible Imputation of Missing Data. CRC Press.
#   Youden WJ (1950). Cancer, 3(1):32-35.
#==============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(mice)
library(pROC)
library(caret)
library(car)
library(splines)

cat("\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("CHUNK 13: POST-LR DIAGNOSTICS (MULTIPLY IMPUTED DATA)\n")
cat("Models: A (Personality) | B (Full) — VSURF interpretation sets\n")
cat("AUC reported from Chunk 12 (per-imputation mean) for consistency\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART A: LOAD SAVED OBJECTS FROM CHUNK 12
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("PART A: Loading Chunk 12 results\n")
cat("───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

if (!file.exists("regression_comparison_results.rds"))

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART B: RE-FIT RAW MODELS ACROSS ALL IMPUTATIONS
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("PART B: Re-fitting raw models across all imputations\n")
cat("───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

formula_A <- as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~", paste(vars_A, collapse = " + ")))
formula_B <- as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~", paste(vars_B, collapse = " + ")))

cat(sprintf("Formula A: %s\n\n", deparse(formula_A)))
cat(sprintf("Formula B: %s\n\n", deparse(formula_B)))

fit_raw_list <- function(formula_obj, data_list, label) {
  lapply(seq_along(data_list), function(i) {
    tryCatch(
      glm(formula_obj, data = data_list[[i]], family = binomial()),
      error = function(e) {
        cat(sprintf("  ⚠️  %s imputation %d failed: %s\n", label, i, e$message))
        NULL
      })
  })
}

fits_A <- fit_raw_list(formula_A, imputed_list, "Model A")
fits_B <- fit_raw_list(formula_B, imputed_list, "Model B")

n_ok_A <- sum(!sapply(fits_A, is.null))
n_ok_B <- sum(!sapply(fits_B, is.null))
cat(sprintf("✓ Model A: %d / %d imputations fitted successfully\n",   n_ok_A, m))
cat(sprintf("✓ Model B: %d / %d imputations fitted successfully\n\n", n_ok_B, m))

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART C: NAGELKERKE R2 — MANUAL COMPUTATION PER IMPUTATION
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART C: Nagelkerke R² (manual computation per imputation)\n")
cat("Ref: Nagelkerke (1991); van Buuren (2018)\n")
cat("NOTE: pool.r.squared() not used — does not support GLM objects\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

nagelkerke_manual <- function(fits_list, data_list, outcome_var, label) {

  r2_vals <- sapply(seq_along(fits_list), function(i) {
    fit <- fits_list[[i]]
    if (is.null(fit)) return(NA_real_)
    n        <- nrow(data_list[[i]])
    ll_full  <- as.numeric(logLik(fit))
    null_fit <- glm(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ 1")),
                    data = data_list[[i]], family = binomial())
    ll_null  <- as.numeric(logLik(null_fit))
    r2_cox   <- 1 - exp((ll_null - ll_full) * (2 / n))
    r2_max   <- 1 - exp(ll_null * (2 / n))
    if (r2_max == 0) return(NA_real_)
    r2_cox / r2_max
  })

  valid   <- r2_vals[!is.na(r2_vals)]
  mean_r2 <- mean(valid)
  sd_r2   <- sd(valid)

  cat(sprintf("%s:\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (mean across %d imputations): %.4f\n",
              length(valid), mean_r2))
  cat(sprintf("  SD across imputations: %.4f\n", sd_r2))
  cat(sprintf("  Range: %.4f – %.4f\n\n", min(valid), max(valid)))

  list(mean = mean_r2, sd = sd_r2, min = min(valid),
       max = max(valid), per_imputation = r2_vals)
}

r2_A <- nagelkerke_manual(fits_A, imputed_list, outcome_var, "Model A — Personality")
r2_B <- nagelkerke_manual(fits_B, imputed_list, outcome_var, "Model B — Full")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART D: HOSMER-LEMESHOW TEST — MANUAL MI POOLING
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART D: Hosmer-Lemeshow test (mean chi-square across imputations)\n")
cat("g = 10 decile groups; df = 8\n")
cat("Ref: Hosmer & Lemeshow (2000); Enders (2010)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

hl_mi <- function(fits_list, data_list, outcome_var, g = 10, label) {

  mm        <- length(fits_list)
  chi2_vals <- rep(NA_real_, mm)
  df_val    <- g - 2L

  for (i in seq_len(mm)) {
    if (is.null(fits_list[[i]])) next
    pred <- predict(fits_list[[i]], type = "response")
    obs  <- as.integer(data_list[[i]][[outcome_var]])

    breaks    <- quantile(pred, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = g + 1), na.rm = TRUE)
    breaks[1] <- breaks[1] - 1e-10
    groups    <- cut(pred, breaks = breaks, labels = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE)

    obs_1  <- tapply(obs,  groups, sum,    na.rm = TRUE)
    exp_1  <- tapply(pred, groups, sum,    na.rm = TRUE)
    n_g    <- tapply(obs,  groups, length)
    obs_0  <- n_g - obs_1
    exp_0  <- n_g - exp_1

    valid_cells  <- exp_1 > 0 & exp_0 > 0
    chi2_vals[i] <- sum(
      ((obs_1 - exp_1)^2 / exp_1 + (obs_0 - exp_0)^2 / exp_0)[valid_cells],
      na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  valid     <- !is.na(chi2_vals)
  chi2_pool <- mean(chi2_vals[valid])
  p_pool    <- pchisq(chi2_pool, df = df_val, lower.tail = FALSE)
  n_valid   <- sum(valid)

  cat(sprintf("%s:\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  Groups (g):          %d\n",    g))
  cat(sprintf("  df:                  %d  (g - 2)\n", df_val))
  cat(sprintf("  Imputations used:    %d / %d\n", n_valid, mm))
  cat(sprintf("  Pooled chi-square:   %.4f\n",  chi2_pool))
  cat(sprintf("  p-value:             %.4f  %s\n\n",
              p_pool,
              ifelse(p_pool >= 0.05, "✓ Adequate fit (p >= .05)",
                                     "⚠️  Poor fit (p < .05)")))

  list(chi2 = chi2_pool, df = df_val, p = p_pool,
       g = g, n_valid = n_valid, chi2_per_imp = chi2_vals)
}

hl_A <- hl_mi(fits_A, imputed_list, outcome_var, g = 10, "Model A — Personality")
hl_B <- hl_mi(fits_B, imputed_list, outcome_var, g = 10, "Model B — Full")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART E: CONFUSION MATRIX — YOUDEN-OPTIMAL THRESHOLD
#   AUC reported is the Chunk 12 per-imputation mean (for consistency).
#   The pooled-prediction ROC is used ONLY to choose the Youden threshold.
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART E: Confusion matrix (Youden-optimal threshold)\n")
cat("AUC = Chunk 12 per-imputation mean; threshold from pooled predictions.\n")
cat("Ref: Youden (1950); Klok et al. (2022)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

pool_predictions <- function(fits_list, data_list) {
  preds <- lapply(seq_along(fits_list), function(i) {
    if (is.null(fits_list[[i]])) return(NULL)
    predict(fits_list[[i]], newdata = data_list[[i]], type = "response")
  })
  valid_preds <- Filter(Negate(is.null), preds)
  Reduce("+", valid_preds) / length(valid_preds)
}

avg_pred_A <- pool_predictions(fits_A, imputed_list)
avg_pred_B <- pool_predictions(fits_B, imputed_list)
observed   <- imputed_list[[1]][[outcome_var]]

run_confusion_matrix <- function(avg_pred, obs, label, auc_ch12 = NULL) {
  cat(sprintf("%s:\n", label))

  roc_obj     <- roc(obs, avg_pred, quiet = TRUE)
  best        <- coords(roc_obj, "best",
                        ret         = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity"),
                        best.method = "youden",
                        transpose   = FALSE)
  best_thresh <- best$threshold[1]

  if (!is.null(auc_ch12)) {
    auc_val       <- auc_ch12$AUC_mean[1]
    auc_formatted <- auc_ch12$AUC_formatted[1]
    auc_source    <- "Chunk 12 per-imputation mean"
  } else {
    auc_val       <- as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
    auc_formatted <- sprintf("%.3f", auc_val)
    auc_source    <- "pooled predictions (Chunk 12 AUC unavailable)"
  }

  cat(sprintf("  AUC (%s): %s\n", auc_source, auc_formatted))
  cat(sprintf("  Youden's J threshold (from pooled predictions): %.4f\n", best_thresh))

  pred_class <- factor(ifelse(avg_pred >= best_thresh, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
  obs_factor <- factor(obs, levels = c(0, 1))
  cm         <- confusionMatrix(pred_class, obs_factor, positive = "1")

  print(cm$table)
  cat("\n")

  sens <- round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"],    3)
  spec <- round(cm$byClass["Specificity"],    3)
  ppv  <- round(cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"], 3)
  npv  <- round(cm$byClass["Neg Pred Value"], 3)
  acc  <- round(cm$overall["Accuracy"],       3)

  cat(sprintf("  Sensitivity:   %.3f\n", sens))
  cat(sprintf("  Specificity:   %.3f\n", spec))
  cat(sprintf("  PPV:           %.3f\n", ppv))
  cat(sprintf("  NPV:           %.3f\n", npv))
  cat(sprintf("  Accuracy:      %.3f\n", acc))
  cat(sprintf("  Threshold:     %.4f (Youden's J)\n\n", best_thresh))

  list(auc = auc_val, auc_formatted = auc_formatted, threshold = best_thresh,
       sensitivity = sens, specificity = spec, ppv = ppv, npv = npv,
       accuracy = acc, cm_table = cm$table, cm_full = cm)
}

cm_A <- run_confusion_matrix(avg_pred_A, observed, "Model A — Personality", auc12_A)
cm_B <- run_confusion_matrix(avg_pred_B, observed, "Model B — Full",        auc12_B)

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART F: BOX-TIDWELL TEST — LINEARITY IN THE LOGIT
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART F: Box-Tidwell test — linearity in the logit\n")
cat("Imputation 1 only; Bonferroni correction applied.\n")
cat("Variables with min <= 0 shifted by +1 before log transformation.\n")
cat("Ref: Box & Tidwell (1962); Harrell (2015); van Buuren (2018)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

dat_bt <- imputed_list[[1]]

run_box_tidwell <- function(outcome, all_vars, cont_vars, data, label) {
  cat(sprintf("%s:\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  Continuous predictors tested (%d): %s\n",
              length(cont_vars), paste(cont_vars, collapse = ", ")))

  bonferroni_alpha <- 0.05 / max(length(cont_vars), 1)
  cat(sprintf("  Bonferroni-corrected alpha: %.4f (0.05 / %d)\n\n",
              bonferroni_alpha, length(cont_vars)))

  if (length(cont_vars) == 0) {
    cat("  No continuous predictors — Box-Tidwell not applicable.\n\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  dat_test  <- data
  shift_log <- list()
  for (v in cont_vars) {
    min_v <- min(dat_test[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
    if (min_v <= 0) {
      shift          <- abs(min_v) + 1
      dat_test[[v]]  <- dat_test[[v]] + shift
      shift_log[[v]] <- shift
      cat(sprintf("  ℹ️  '%s' shifted by +%.2f for log (min <= 0)\n", v, shift))
    }
  }
  if (length(shift_log) > 0) cat("\n")

  bt_terms   <- paste(sprintf("I(%s * log(%s))", cont_vars, cont_vars), collapse = " + ")
  bt_formula <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, "~", paste(all_vars, collapse = " + "), "+", bt_terms))

  bt_fit <- tryCatch(
    glm(bt_formula, data = dat_test, family = binomial()),
    error = function(e) {
      cat(sprintf("  ✗ Box-Tidwell model failed: %s\n\n", e$message))
      NULL
    })
  if (is.null(bt_fit)) return(NULL)

  coef_tbl <- summary(bt_fit)$coefficients
  bt_rows  <- grep("log\\(", rownames(coef_tbl))

  if (length(bt_rows) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠️  No interaction terms found in model output.\n\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  bt_results <- coef_tbl[bt_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  bt_df <- data.frame(
    Term     = rownames(bt_results),
    Estimate = round(bt_results[, "Estimate"],   4),
    SE       = round(bt_results[, "Std. Error"], 4),
    z_value  = round(bt_results[, "z value"],    3),
    p_value  = round(bt_results[, "Pr(>|z|)"],   4),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Significant_Bonferroni = p_value < bonferroni_alpha,
      Interpretation = ifelse(
        Significant_Bonferroni,
        "⚠️  NON-LINEAR — consider polynomial or spline",
        "✓ Linear assumption met"))

  cat("  Box-Tidwell interaction terms (X*log(X)):\n")
  print(bt_df, row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("\n  Bonferroni-corrected alpha: %.4f\n", bonferroni_alpha))

  violations <- bt_df$Term[bt_df$Significant_Bonferroni]
  if (length(violations) == 0) {
    cat("  ✓ No violations. Linearity in the logit supported.\n\n")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("  ⚠️  %d violation(s):\n", length(violations)))
    for (v in violations) cat(sprintf("     • %s\n", v))
    cat("  Consider polynomial terms or restricted cubic splines.\n\n")
  }

  list(results = bt_df, alpha_bonferroni = bonferroni_alpha,
       violations = violations, shifts = shift_log)
}

bt_A <- run_box_tidwell(outcome_var, vars_A, cont_A, dat_bt, "Model A — Personality")
bt_B <- run_box_tidwell(outcome_var, vars_B, cont_B, dat_bt, "Model B — Full")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART F2: DBAS_Medications NONLINEARITY SENSITIVITY CHECK (SUPPLEMENTARY)
#   Box-Tidwell flagged DBAS_Medications in Model A only; Model B was clean.
#   Refit Model A with DBAS_Medications as a natural cubic spline (df = 3) and
#   test whether it materially changes discrimination, i.e. whether the linear
#   term is an adequate approximation despite the flag. Run across imputations.
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART F2: DBAS_Medications linear vs spline sensitivity (Model A)\n")
cat("Supplementary — addresses the Box-Tidwell flag in Model A\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

bt_term   <- "DBAS_Medications"
dbas_sens <- NULL

if (bt_term %in% vars_A) {

  spl_form_A <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome_var, "~",
          paste(ifelse(vars_A == bt_term, sprintf("ns(%s, df = 3)", bt_term), vars_A),
                collapse = " + ")))

  auc_lin <- auc_spl <- lrt_p <- rep(NA_real_, m)
  for (i in seq_len(m)) {
    fit_l <- tryCatch(glm(formula_A,  data = imputed_list[[i]], family = binomial()),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
    fit_s <- tryCatch(glm(spl_form_A, data = imputed_list[[i]], family = binomial()),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit_l) || is.null(fit_s)) next
    obs        <- imputed_list[[i]][[outcome_var]]
    auc_lin[i] <- as.numeric(auc(roc(obs, predict(fit_l, type = "response"), quiet = TRUE)))
    auc_spl[i] <- as.numeric(auc(roc(obs, predict(fit_s, type = "response"), quiet = TRUE)))
    lrt_p[i]   <- anova(fit_l, fit_s, test = "LRT")[2, "Pr(>Chi)"]
  }

  mean_auc_lin <- mean(auc_lin, na.rm = TRUE)
  mean_auc_spl <- mean(auc_spl, na.rm = TRUE)
  delta_auc    <- mean(auc_spl - auc_lin, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_lrt_sig    <- sum(lrt_p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

  cat(sprintf("  Mean AUC, linear DBAS_Medications:    %.3f\n", mean_auc_lin))
  cat(sprintf("  Mean AUC, spline DBAS_Medications:    %.3f\n", mean_auc_spl))
  cat(sprintf("  Mean change in AUC (spline - linear): %+.4f\n", delta_auc))
  cat(sprintf("  LRT significant (p < .05) in %d of %d imputations\n\n", n_lrt_sig, m))
  cat("  Interpretation: a small AUC change indicates the linear term is an\n")
  cat("  adequate approximation for discrimination despite the Box-Tidwell\n")
  cat("  flag. Model B showed no nonlinearity. See Chunk 9B for the\n")
  cat("  linear-vs-spline logit figure for DBAS_Medications.\n\n")

  dbas_sens <- list(term = bt_term, mean_auc_linear = mean_auc_lin,
                    mean_auc_spline = mean_auc_spl, delta_auc = delta_auc,
                    lrt_p = lrt_p, n_lrt_sig = n_lrt_sig)

} else {
  cat(sprintf("  '%s' not in Model A — sensitivity check skipped.\n\n", bt_term))
}

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART G: Class imbalance\n")
cat("Ref: Klok et al. (2022). JAMIA. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocac093\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

n_0         <- as.integer(tbl["0"])

cat(sprintf("  Stoppers   (= 1): %d  (%.1f%%)\n", n_1, 100 * prop_tbl["1"]))
cat(sprintf("  Continuers (= 0): %d  (%.1f%%)\n", n_0, 100 * prop_tbl["0"]))
cat(sprintf("  Majority:minority ratio: %.2f : 1\n\n", ratio))

if (ratio >= 3) {
  cat("⚠️  Imbalance detected (ratio >= 3:1).\n")
} else {
  cat("✓ Mild imbalance (ratio < 3:1).\n")
}
cat("  No resampling correction applied — Klok et al. (2022) justification.\n")
cat("  Threshold optimised via Youden's J index (Part E).\n\n")

r2_val_A  <- if (!is.null(r2_A)) round(r2_A$mean, 4) else NA

summary_tbl <- data.frame(

    "HL interpretation",
    "AUC (Chunk 12 mean [95% CI])",
    "Operating threshold (Youden)",

    "Specificity",
    "PPV",
    "NPV",
    "Accuracy",
    "Box-Tidwell violations",
    "Class imbalance ratio"),
  Model_A = c(
    ifelse(is.na(r2_val_A),  "NA", as.character(r2_val_A)),
    ifelse(is.na(hl_chi2_A), "NA", as.character(hl_chi2_A)),
    ifelse(is.na(hl_p_A),    "NA", as.character(hl_p_A)),
    ifelse(is.na(hl_p_A),    "NA", ifelse(hl_p_A >= 0.05, "Adequate", "Poor")),
    cm_A$auc_formatted,
    as.character(round(cm_A$threshold, 4)),

    as.character(cm_A$ppv),
    as.character(cm_A$npv),

    bt_viol_A,
    sprintf("%.2f:1", ratio)),
  Model_B = c(
    ifelse(is.na(r2_val_B),  "NA", as.character(r2_val_B)),
    ifelse(is.na(hl_chi2_B), "NA", as.character(hl_chi2_B)),
    ifelse(is.na(hl_p_B),    "NA", as.character(hl_p_B)),
    ifelse(is.na(hl_p_B),    "NA", ifelse(hl_p_B >= 0.05, "Adequate", "Poor")),
    cm_B$auc_formatted,
    as.character(round(cm_B$threshold, 4)),
    as.character(cm_B$sensitivity),
    as.character(cm_B$specificity),
    as.character(cm_B$ppv),
    as.character(cm_B$npv),
    as.character(cm_B$accuracy),
    bt_viol_B,
    sprintf("%.2f:1", ratio)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

print(summary_tbl, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART J (SENSITIVITY): DeLong with a correctly specified (spline) Model A
#   Part F2 showed DBAS_Medications is nonlinear in Model A (LRT significant
#   in every imputation). The Chunk 12 DeLong compared a LINEAR Model A
#   against Model B, so the comparator was under-specified. Here we refit
#   Model A with ns(DBAS_Medications, df = 3), leave Model B unchanged, and
#   re-run the pooled DeLong (Rubin's rules on delta-AUC, Li & Fine 2010) to
#   check whether the full model's advantage survives a fair comparator.
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART J (SENSITIVITY): DeLong — spline Model A vs Model B\n")
cat("Model A refit with ns(DBAS_Medications, df = 3); Model B unchanged.\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

bt_term       <- "DBAS_Medications"
delong_spline <- NULL

if (!(bt_term %in% vars_A)) {
  cat(sprintf("  '%s' not in Model A — sensitivity DeLong skipped.\n\n", bt_term))
} else {

  spl_form_A <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome_var, "~",
          paste(ifelse(vars_A == bt_term, sprintf("ns(%s, df = 3)", bt_term), vars_A),
                collapse = " + ")))

  fits_A_spl <- fit_raw_list(spl_form_A, imputed_list, "Model A (spline)")

  delong_s <- vector("list", m)
  for (i in seq_len(m)) {
    if (is.null(fits_A_spl[[i]]) || is.null(fits_B[[i]])) {
      delong_s[[i]] <- list(delta = NA_real_, var = NA_real_,
                            auc_A = NA_real_, auc_B = NA_real_)
      next
    }
    obs_i    <- imputed_list[[i]][[outcome_var]]
    roc_A_i  <- roc(obs_i, predict(fits_A_spl[[i]], type = "response"), quiet = TRUE)
    roc_B_i  <- roc(obs_i, predict(fits_B[[i]],     type = "response"), quiet = TRUE)
    auc_A_i  <- as.numeric(auc(roc_A_i))
    auc_B_i  <- as.numeric(auc(roc_B_i))
    delta_i  <- auc_B_i - auc_A_i
    test_i   <- roc.test(roc_A_i, roc_B_i, method = "delong", paired = TRUE)
    z_i      <- as.numeric(test_i$statistic)
    se_i     <- if (abs(z_i) > 1e-8) abs(delta_i / z_i) else abs(delta_i) + 1e-8
    delong_s[[i]] <- list(delta = delta_i, var = se_i^2,
                          auc_A = auc_A_i, auc_B = auc_B_i)
  }

  valid_idx <- which(sapply(delong_s, function(r) !is.na(r$delta)))
  m_valid   <- length(valid_idx)
  if (m_valid == 0) stop("DeLong sensitivity: no valid imputations.")

  delta_vec <- sapply(delong_s[valid_idx], `[[`, "delta")
  var_vec   <- sapply(delong_s[valid_idx], `[[`, "var")

  Q_bar  <- mean(delta_vec)
  U_bar  <- mean(var_vec)
  B      <- var(delta_vec)
  T_var  <- U_bar + (1 + 1 / m_valid) * B
  z_pool <- Q_bar / sqrt(T_var)
  p_pool <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_pool))

  r_L   <- (1 + 1 / m_valid) * B / U_bar
  df_BR <- if (is.finite(r_L) && r_L > 1e-10) (m_valid - 1) / r_L^2 else Inf
  p_t   <- if (is.finite(df_BR)) 2 * pt(-abs(z_pool), df = df_BR) else p_pool

  mean_auc_A_spl <- mean(sapply(delong_s[valid_idx], `[[`, "auc_A"))
  mean_auc_B     <- mean(sapply(delong_s[valid_idx], `[[`, "auc_B"))

  cat(sprintf("  Mean AUC, spline Model A: %.3f\n", mean_auc_A_spl))
  cat(sprintf("  Mean AUC, Model B:        %.3f\n", mean_auc_B))
  cat(sprintf("  Pooled delta-AUC (B - spline A): %+.4f\n", Q_bar))
  cat(sprintf("  SE %.4f | z %.3f | p (normal) %.4f | p (t, df=%.1f) %.4f\n\n",
              sqrt(T_var), z_pool, p_pool, df_BR, p_t))

  if (!is.null(ch12$delong$pooled)) {
    lin <- ch12$delong$pooled
    cat("  Comparison with Chunk 12 (linear Model A):\n")
    cat(sprintf("    Linear A:  delta-AUC %+.4f, z %.3f, p %.4f\n",
                lin$pooled_delta_AUC[1], lin$z_pooled[1], lin$p_normal[1]))
    cat(sprintf("    Spline A:  delta-AUC %+.4f, z %.3f, p %.4f\n\n",
                Q_bar, z_pool, p_pool))
  }

  if (p_pool < 0.05) {
    cat("  ✓ Model B still discriminates significantly better than a correctly\n")
    cat("    specified (spline) Model A. The advantage is robust to the\n")
    cat("    DBAS_Medications nonlinearity.\n\n")
  } else {
    cat("  ⚠️  With a spline-specified Model A the advantage is no longer\n")
    cat("    significant at .05. Report this and lean on Nagelkerke R² and the\n")
    cat("    EFA_F1 / EFA_F2 effects as the primary evidence for the full model.\n\n")
  }

  delong_spline <- list(
    pooled_delta_AUC = Q_bar, SE = sqrt(T_var), z = z_pool,
    p_normal = p_pool, p_t = p_t, df_BR = df_BR,
    mean_auc_A_spline = mean_auc_A_spl, mean_auc_B = mean_auc_B,
    m_valid = m_valid)
}

if (exists("output_ch13")) {
  output_ch13$delong_spline_sensitivity <- delong_spline
  saveRDS(output_ch13, "chunk13_diagnostics_results.rds")
  cat("✓ Updated chunk13_diagnostics_results.rds with delong_spline_sensitivity\n\n")
}

# Nagelkerke R² for the spline-specified Model A (reuses Part J fits)
if (!exists("fits_A_spl")) {
  spl_form_A <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome_var, "~",
          paste(ifelse(vars_A == "DBAS_Medications",
                       "ns(DBAS_Medications, df = 3)", vars_A),
                collapse = " + ")))
  fits_A_spl <- fit_raw_list(spl_form_A, imputed_list, "Model A (spline)")
}

r2_A_spl <- nagelkerke_manual(fits_A_spl, imputed_list, outcome_var,
                              "Model A (spline DBAS_Medications)")

cat("  Nagelkerke R² comparison:\n")
cat(sprintf("    Model A (linear):  %.4f\n", r2_A$mean))
cat(sprintf("    Model A (spline):  %.4f\n", r2_A_spl$mean))
cat(sprintf("    Model B (full):    %.4f\n", r2_B$mean))

if (exists("output_ch13")) {
  output_ch13$nagelkerke$model_A_spline <- r2_A_spl
  saveRDS(output_ch13, "chunk13_diagnostics_results.rds")
}

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART K (NEW): TEN-FOLD STRATIFIED CROSS-VALIDATION
#   Within each of the m imputed datasets, participants are randomly assigned
#   to 10 folds stratified by outcome (stratification keeps the stopper/
#   continuer proportion roughly constant across folds, which matters here
#   given the class imbalance quantified in Part G). The model is refit on 9
#   folds and evaluated on the held-out fold; this repeats until every fold
#   has served once as the validation set. Fold-level AUCs are averaged
#   within each imputation to give one cross-validated AUC per imputation,
#   and those m values are pooled (simple mean/SD; Rubin's rules add little
#   here since cross-validated AUC is already an out-of-sample summary, not
#   a model parameter with its own analytic sampling variance).
#
#   Optimism = apparent AUC (Chunk 12; fit and evaluated on the same data)
#   minus this cross-validated AUC. A small optimism indicates the apparent
#   AUC is not substantially inflated by fitting and evaluating on the same
#   observations.
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART K: Ten-fold cross-validation (stratified by outcome)\n")
cat("Ref: Kohavi (1995); stratified within each of the m imputations\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

set.seed(2026)  # reproducibility of fold assignment; change/remove if you
                # already set a global seed earlier in the pipeline

run_cv <- function(formula_obj, data_list, outcome_var, k = 10, label) {

  cat(sprintf("%s:\n", label))

  fold_auc_by_imp <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(data_list), ncol = k)

  for (i in seq_along(data_list)) {
    dat <- data_list[[i]]
    obs <- dat[[outcome_var]]

    # Stratified fold assignment: shuffle indices within each outcome level,
    # then assign fold labels 1:k in rotation so every fold gets a similar
    # proportion of stoppers and continuers.
    folds <- rep(NA_integer_, nrow(dat))
    for (lvl in unique(obs)) {
      idx        <- which(obs == lvl)
      idx        <- sample(idx)
      folds[idx] <- rep(seq_len(k), length.out = length(idx))
    }

    for (f in seq_len(k)) {
      test_idx  <- which(folds == f)
      train_idx <- which(folds != f)

      fit_f <- tryCatch(
        glm(formula_obj, data = dat[train_idx, ], family = binomial()),
        error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(fit_f)) next

      pred_f <- tryCatch(
        predict(fit_f, newdata = dat[test_idx, ], type = "response"),
        error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, length(test_idx)))

      obs_f <- obs[test_idx]
      if (length(unique(obs_f)) < 2 || all(is.na(pred_f))) next

      auc_f <- tryCatch(
        as.numeric(auc(roc(obs_f, pred_f, quiet = TRUE))),
        error = function(e) NA_real_)

      fold_auc_by_imp[i, f] <- auc_f
    }
  }

  # Mean fold-level AUC within each imputation, then pooled across imputations
  mean_auc_per_imp <- rowMeans(fold_auc_by_imp, na.rm = TRUE)
  cv_auc_mean      <- mean(mean_auc_per_imp, na.rm = TRUE)
  cv_auc_sd        <- sd(mean_auc_per_imp,   na.rm = TRUE)

  # Fold-level stability across imputations
  fold_mean <- colMeans(fold_auc_by_imp, na.rm = TRUE)
  fold_sd   <- apply(fold_auc_by_imp, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)

  cat(sprintf("  Cross-validated AUC (pooled across %d imputations): %.3f (SD = %.3f)\n",
              length(data_list), cv_auc_mean, cv_auc_sd))
  cat(sprintf("  Range across imputations: %.3f - %.3f\n\n",
              min(mean_auc_per_imp, na.rm = TRUE), max(mean_auc_per_imp, na.rm = TRUE)))

  cat("  Fold-level AUC stability (mean, SD across imputations):\n")
  fold_tbl <- data.frame(Fold = seq_len(k),
                         Mean_AUC = round(fold_mean, 3),
                         SD       = round(fold_sd,   3))
  print(fold_tbl, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n")

  list(cv_auc_mean = cv_auc_mean, cv_auc_sd = cv_auc_sd,
       mean_auc_per_imputation = mean_auc_per_imp,
       fold_auc_matrix = fold_auc_by_imp,
       fold_table = fold_tbl, k = k)
}

cv_A <- run_cv(formula_A, imputed_list, outcome_var, k = 10, "Model A — Personality")
cv_B <- run_cv(formula_B, imputed_list, outcome_var, k = 10, "Model B — Full")

# Optimism = apparent (Chunk 12) AUC minus cross-validated AUC
apparent_auc_A <- if (!is.null(auc12_A)) auc12_A$AUC_mean[1] else NA_real_
apparent_auc_B <- if (!is.null(auc12_B)) auc12_B$AUC_mean[1] else NA_real_
optimism_A     <- apparent_auc_A - cv_A$cv_auc_mean
optimism_B     <- apparent_auc_B - cv_B$cv_auc_mean

cat("OPTIMISM (apparent AUC minus cross-validated AUC):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Model A: apparent %.3f - CV %.3f = optimism %+.4f\n",
            apparent_auc_A, cv_A$cv_auc_mean, optimism_A))
cat(sprintf("  Model B: apparent %.3f - CV %.3f = optimism %+.4f\n\n",
            apparent_auc_B, cv_B$cv_auc_mean, optimism_B))
cat("  Interpretation: small optimism (e.g., < .03-.05) indicates the\n")
cat("  apparent AUC is not substantially inflated by evaluating the model\n")
cat("  on the same data it was fit to.\n\n")

# Append cross-validation rows onto the Part H summary table
summary_tbl <- rbind(
  summary_tbl,
  data.frame(
    Diagnostic = c("Cross-validated AUC (10-fold, pooled)",
                   "Optimism (apparent - CV)"),
    Model_A = c(sprintf("%.3f (SD %.3f)", cv_A$cv_auc_mean, cv_A$cv_auc_sd),
               sprintf("%+.4f", optimism_A)),
    Model_B = c(sprintf("%.3f (SD %.3f)", cv_B$cv_auc_mean, cv_B$cv_auc_sd),
               sprintf("%+.4f", optimism_B)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE))

cat("Updated diagnostic summary (with cross-validation):\n")
print(summary_tbl, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART I: SAVE ALL RESULTS
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("PART I: Saving results\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

output_ch13 <- list(

  nagelkerke = list(model_A = r2_A, model_B = r2_B,
                    model_A_spline = r2_A_spl),

  hosmer_lemeshow = list(model_A = hl_A, model_B = hl_B),

  confusion_matrix = list(model_A = cm_A, model_B = cm_B),

  box_tidwell = list(model_A = bt_A, model_B = bt_B),

  dbas_med_sensitivity = dbas_sens,

  delong_spline_sensitivity = delong_spline,

  cross_validation = list(
    model_A  = cv_A,
    model_B  = cv_B,
    optimism = list(model_A = optimism_A, model_B = optimism_B,
                    apparent_auc_A = apparent_auc_A,
                    apparent_auc_B = apparent_auc_B)),

  class_imbalance = list(
    table = tbl, proportions = prop_tbl,
    n_stoppers = n_1, n_continuers = n_0, ratio = ratio),

  summary_table = summary_tbl,

  metadata = list(
    outcome           = outcome_var,
    auc_source        = "Chunk 12 per-imputation mean (reported); pooled predictions used only for Youden threshold",
    threshold_method  = "Youden's J index",
    hl_method         = "Mean chi-square across imputations (g=10, df=8)",
    nagelkerke_method = "Manual per imputation, averaged (Nagelkerke 1991)",
    bt_imputation     = 1,

    f2_note           = "Part F2: DBAS_Medications linear vs natural cubic spline (Model A)",
    cv_method         = "10-fold, stratified by outcome, within each of the m imputations; folds pooled by simple mean/SD across imputations",
    cv_seed           = 2026,
    resampling        = "None — Klok et al. (2022) justification",
    vars_A = vars_A, vars_B = vars_B, cont_A = cont_A, cont_B = cont_B,
    m = m, N = N,
    references = c(
      "Box & Tidwell (1962). Technometrics, 4(4):531-550.",
      "Enders CK (2010). Applied Missing Data Analysis.",
      "Harrell FE (2015). Regression Modeling Strategies (2nd ed.).",
      "Hosmer & Lemeshow (2000). Applied Logistic Regression (2nd ed.).",
      "Klok et al. (2022). JAMIA. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocac093",
      "Kohavi R (1995). IJCAI, 14(2):1137-1145.",
      "Nagelkerke NJD (1991). Biometrika, 78(3):691-692.",
      "Rubin DB (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys.",
      "van Buuren S (2018). Flexible Imputation of Missing Data.",
      "Youden WJ (1950). Cancer, 3(1):32-35.")))

saveRDS(output_ch13, "chunk13_diagnostics_results.rds")
write_csv(summary_tbl, "chunk13_diagnostic_summary.csv")

if (!is.null(bt_A) && !is.null(bt_A$results))
  write_csv(bt_A$results, "chunk13_boxtidwell_A.csv")
if (!is.null(bt_B) && !is.null(bt_B$results))
  write_csv(bt_B$results, "chunk13_boxtidwell_B.csv")

write_csv(cv_A$fold_table, "chunk13_cv_fold_table_A.csv")
write_csv(cv_B$fold_table, "chunk13_cv_fold_table_B.csv")

cat("✓ Saved: chunk13_diagnostics_results.rds\n")
cat("✓ Saved: chunk13_diagnostic_summary.csv\n")
if (!is.null(bt_A) && !is.null(bt_A$results))
  cat("✓ Saved: chunk13_boxtidwell_A.csv\n")
if (!is.null(bt_B) && !is.null(bt_B$results))
  cat("✓ Saved: chunk13_boxtidwell_B.csv\n")
cat("✓ Saved: chunk13_cv_fold_table_A.csv\n")
cat("✓ Saved: chunk13_cv_fold_table_B.csv\n")
cat("\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FINAL SUMMARY
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("CHUNK 13 COMPLETE\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("KEY RESULTS:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Nagelkerke R²:  A=%.4f  B=%.4f\n",
            ifelse(is.na(r2_val_A), NA, r2_val_A),
            ifelse(is.na(r2_val_B), NA, r2_val_B)))
cat(sprintf("  HL p-value:     A=%.4f (%s)  B=%.4f (%s)\n",
```

## Influential Cases

```{r}
#==============================================================================
# CHUNK 14: INFLUENTIAL CASES ANALYSIS — MODEL A & MODEL B
#==============================================================================
# Purpose:
#   Characterizes and assess' the robustness of influential cases separately
#   for Model A (Personality, interpretation set) and Model B (Full,
#   interpretation set).
#
# PUBLICATION VERSION:
#   Model B contains the EFA-derived discontinuation-cognition factors
#   (EFA_F1, EFA_F2), which exist only in imputed_datasets_efa_scales.rds
#   (the EFA chunk output). This chunk therefore loads that file rather than
#   imputed_datasets_complete_final.rds. Variable sets and raw-score
#   coefficient summaries are read from regression_comparison_results.rds
#   (publication Chunk 12). Output filenames match the thesis version, so run
#   this in a SEPARATE working directory to avoid overwriting thesis outputs.
#
# HOW COOK'S D IS CALCULATED:
#   Cook's distance (Cook, 1977) measures how much all fitted values change
#   when a single observation is deleted from the model. For logistic
#   regression, it is approximated as:
#
#     D_i = (h_ii / (p * (1 - h_ii)^2)) * r_i^2
#
#   where:
#     h_ii   = leverage of observation i (diagonal of the hat matrix),
#              reflecting how far i's predictor values are from the centroid
#     r_i    = Pearson residual for observation i — how far the observed
#              outcome is from the model's predicted probability
#     p      = number of parameters (including intercept)
#
#   Intuitively: Cook's D is large when an observation has BOTH unusual
#   predictor values (high leverage) AND a poor fit (large residual).
#   Either alone is not sufficient — a high-leverage point that is well
#   predicted has small D; a poorly-predicted point at the centroid of X
#   also has small D.
#
#   Across multiple imputations, Cook's D is computed separately on each
#   imputed dataset (because the imputed values of missing predictors differ
#   across datasets, so leverage and residuals will vary slightly). The MEAN
#   Cook's D across all m imputations is used to flag cases, which is more
#   stable than a single-imputation estimate. The min-max range across
#   imputations indicates how consistently a case is influential: a small
#   range means the case is influential regardless of which imputed values
#   it received, strengthening the conclusion that its influence is real
#   rather than a product of a single imputation's values.
#
#   Threshold: 4/N (Cook & Weisberg, 1982). Cases whose MEAN Cook's D
#   exceeds this threshold are flagged as influential.
#
# Influential case identification:
#   Cook's D computed per imputation; mean Cook's D averaged across all
#   imputations. Cases with mean Cook's D > 4/N flagged as influential.
#   The same case IDs are removed consistently from all datasets for
#   the removal sensitivity analysis.
#
# Descriptive profiling (Parts C-F):
#   Continuous variables: statistics pooled across all imputations.
#   Factor variables (e.g. stop_wdl_exp_combined): frequency counts and
#   percentages per level, pooled across imputations. Pooled t-tests
#   replaced by Fisher's exact test for factors.
#
# Scenario classification (Part F):
#   Data-driven thresholds (pooled across imputations):
#   - Continuous: predictor flagged if inf/non-inf top OR bottom quartile
#     rate ratio >= 1.5 (directional).
#   - Factor: predictor flagged if ANY level has inf/non-inf prevalence
#     ratio >= 1.5. Flagged level(s) reported.
#   Scenario assigned by proportion of flagged predictors:
#     >= 75% flagged -> Scenario 1 (coherent clinical subgroup)
#     25-74% flagged -> Scenario 2 (partial / heterogeneous)
#     <  25% flagged -> Scenario 3 (statistical outliers)
#
# Removal sensitivity (Part G):
#   Model refit on all imputed datasets with influential cases removed.
#   Coefficients pooled using manual Rubin's rules.
#   Pooled ORs compared to Chunk 12 RAW pooled ORs (model_A_raw /
#   model_B_raw from regression_comparison_results.rds).
#   NOTE: term column cast to character before joining to avoid Factor
#   mismatch with pool_glm_manual output (which returns character terms).
#
# Overlap analysis (Parts H-I):
#   Three groups of influential cases are distinguished:
#     - Overlap: cases influential in BOTH Model A and Model B
#     - A-only:  cases influential in Model A but not Model B
#     - B-only:  cases influential in Model B but not Model A
#
#   Overlap cases are the most analytically important: they exert undue
#   influence regardless of predictor domain, suggesting their influence
#   is not domain-specific but reflects something fundamental about those
#   participants (e.g. extreme outcome values, sparse covariate profiles).
#
#   Part H: Standard four-group overlap analysis (Cook's D, outcome rates,
#           predictor profiles across all four groups).
#
#   Part I (new): Overlap-specific deep-dive.
#     I1. Why do overlap cases appear in both models?
#         Compares Cook's D between overlap and single-model cases per model.
#         High D in both models indicates domain-general influence.
#     I2. What distinguishes A-only from B-only influential cases?
#         Profiles predictors unique to each model for that model's
#         single-model influential cases. Tests whether A-only cases are
#         unusual on personality predictors and B-only cases unusual on
#         non-personality predictors (here, the EFA factors and BZRA-use
#         variables that distinguish Model B).
#     I3. Do overlap cases disproportionately drive non-robust findings?
#         Refits each model after removing overlap cases only and checks
#         whether non-robust predictors from Part G lose significance.
#         If yes, the non-robust finding is anchored to the overlap group
#         rather than to the full influential set.
#
# Robustness classification:
#   When separation_flag = TRUE AND m_converged = 0, classified as non-robust.
#   When separation_flag = TRUE AND m_converged >= 1, classified as
#   "Separation in reduced sample — interpret cautiously".
#
# References:
#   Cook RD (1977). Detection of influential observations. Technometrics.
#   Cook RD, Weisberg S (1982). Residuals and Influence in Regression.
#   Rubin DB (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys.
#==============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(pROC)
library(mice)
library(broom)
library(car)

cat("\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("CHUNK 14: INFLUENTIAL CASES ANALYSIS\n")
cat("Model A (Personality) and Model B (Full) — interpretation set\n")
cat("Raw-score models used (consistent with Chunk 12)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

cat("Cook's D measures how much all fitted values change when a single\n")
cat("observation is deleted. It combines leverage (how unusual the\n")
cat("predictor values are) with residual size (how poorly the model\n")
cat("predicts that observation): D_i = (h_ii / (p*(1-h_ii)^2)) * r_i^2.\n")
cat("Computed per imputation; mean D across all imputations used for\n")
cat("flagging. Min-max range across imputations indicates stability.\n")
cat("Threshold: 4/N (Cook & Weisberg, 1982).\n\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PRINT HELPER — formats data frames as plain text via cat() only.
# Never calls print() or capture.output(), both of which RStudio intercepts
# and routes to the viewer pane in notebook/script contexts.
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
print_df <- function(df) {
  df  <- as.data.frame(df)
  nms <- names(df)

  char_df <- as.data.frame(
    lapply(df, function(x) {
      if (is.numeric(x)) {
        formatted <- formatC(x, format = "g", digits = 5)
        ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", formatted)
      } else {
        ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", as.character(x))
      }
    }),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  names(char_df) <- nms

  widths <- mapply(function(col_name, col_vals) {
    max(nchar(col_name), max(nchar(col_vals), na.rm = TRUE))
  }, nms, char_df, SIMPLIFY = TRUE)

  header <- paste(mapply(formatC, nms,      width = widths, flag = "-"), collapse = "  ")
  sep    <- paste(mapply(function(w) paste(rep("-", w), collapse = ""),
                         widths), collapse = "  ")

  cat(header, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n")

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(char_df))) {
    row_str <- paste(mapply(formatC, as.character(char_df[i, ]),
                            width = widths, flag = "-"), collapse = "  ")
    cat(row_str, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\n")
}

cat("PART A: Loading data and Chunk 12 results\n")
cat("───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")

# PUBLICATION: load the EFA-augmented imputed datasets. Model B's predictors
# (EFA_F1, EFA_F2) live only here, so the thesis file would fail every Model B
# fit. Run this in a separate folder; outputs share the thesis filenames.
if (!file.exists("imputed_datasets_efa_scales.rds"))
  stop("ERROR: imputed_datasets_efa_scales.rds not found. Run the EFA chunk first.")

imputed_list <- readRDS("imputed_datasets_efa_scales.rds")
m            <- length(imputed_list)
N            <- nrow(imputed_list[[1]])

if (m != 24)
  warning(sprintf("Expected 24 imputations but found %d.", m))

if (!file.exists("regression_comparison_results.rds"))
  stop("ERROR: regression_comparison_results.rds not found. Run Chunk 12 first.")

chunk12     <- readRDS("regression_comparison_results.rds")
vars_A      <- chunk12$variables$model_A
vars_B      <- chunk12$variables$model_B
outcome_var <- chunk12$metadata$outcome

# Guard: every modelled predictor must exist in the loaded data. Model B now
# carries the EFA factors, so this catches a wrong/stale data file early with
# a clear message instead of a cascade of failed glm fits.
missing_vars <- setdiff(unique(c(vars_A, vars_B, outcome_var)),
                        names(imputed_list[[1]]))
if (length(missing_vars) > 0)
  stop("ERROR: variables missing from imputed data (",
       paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", "),
       "). Did you load imputed_datasets_efa_scales.rds and run the EFA chunk?")

# FIX: Chunk 12 (updated) stores raw-score summaries under model_A_raw and
# model_B_raw. Cast term to character to avoid Factor/character join issues
# in pool_glm_manual downstream.
chunk12$summaries$model_A_raw <- chunk12$summaries$model_A_raw %>%
  mutate(term = as.character(term))
chunk12$summaries$model_B_raw <- chunk12$summaries$model_B_raw %>%
  mutate(term = as.character(term))

formula_A <- as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~", paste(vars_A, collapse = " + ")))
formula_B <- as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~", paste(vars_B, collapse = " + ")))

threshold <- 4 / N

is_factor_var <- function(vars, data) {
  sapply(vars, function(v) is.factor(data[[v]]))
}
factor_flags_A <- is_factor_var(vars_A, imputed_list[[1]])
factor_flags_B <- is_factor_var(vars_B, imputed_list[[1]])

cat(sprintf("✓ Loaded imputed_datasets_efa_scales.rds  (m=%d, N=%d)\n", m, N))
cat(sprintf("✓ Loaded regression_comparison_results.rds\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Using raw-score summaries: model_A_raw / model_B_raw\n\n"))
cat(sprintf("Outcome: %s\n", outcome_var))
cat(sprintf("Cook's D threshold: %.5f  (4 / %d)\n\n", threshold, N))
cat(sprintf("Model A predictors (%d): %s\n", length(vars_A),
            paste(vars_A, collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("  Factor variables: %s\n\n",
            if (any(factor_flags_A)) paste(vars_A[factor_flags_A], collapse = ", ")
            else "none"))
cat(sprintf("Model B predictors (%d): %s\n", length(vars_B),
            paste(vars_B, collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("  Factor variables: %s\n\n",
            if (any(factor_flags_B)) paste(vars_B[factor_flags_B], collapse = ", ")
```
